role: 生成前题材草案；不是逐张实发调用记录。完整实发prompt、实际图片输入与候选选择见sources/*.json。
common: Use case: historical-scene. Asset type: one standalone game city-map building sprite for the tianshu Ming Jiangnan kit. Match the two Southern Song building style references already visible in conversation: finely resolved real clay tiles, stone plinths and wood grain, restrained warm daylight, believable hand-built construction, clean miniature-scale readable silhouette and same detail density. This is a NEW original building, not a copy or edit of those references. Ming Jiangnan palette: chalk-white lime plaster, dark charcoal-grey plain fired clay roof tiles, weathered dark-brown timber, pale grey stone. Authentic restrained south-China timber proportions and gently upturned eaves, no Qing imperial ornament. Camera: STRICT orthographic 2:1 dimetric, yaw 45 degrees, elevation 30 degrees; all ground-plane straight lines slope exactly +0.5 or -0.5; verticals vertical, opposite sides parallel, no perspective convergence. For footprint W by H in metres, the ground diamond is defined by left=(0,16*H), back=(32*H,0), right=(32*(W+H),16*W), front=(32*W,16*(W+H)); show the outer footprint corners clearly, ground only within the footprint, no raised island. Main entrance faces lower-left screen edge. Light from upper-left, tiny soft contact shadow toward lower-right, no wide baked shadow. TRUE transparent RGBA background, all outside regions alpha zero; no painted checkerboard, white background, text, signs, pseudo-writing, people, modern object, sky, neighboring buildings, border, grid, watermark. Full roof eaves, foundations and tiny contact shadow fully visible with generous clear margins. One isolated building or unified compound only.
types: Ming Jiangnan county administrative yamen compound, one main austere hall at the rear, subordinate side offices, formal low entry gate and enclosing white lime walls. Five-bay main hall in dark timber with grey tiled roof, one drum by doorway as a functional clue. Formal balanced paved courtyard, no imperial yellow or red roof. Ground footprint 16 by 13.

Ming Jiangnan escort freight guild compound (original wuxia expansion, not a named historical firm), strong white walls, a large dark timber two-leaf gateway, rear grey-tile cargo hall, side storage sheds, carefully stacked crates and covered bales wholly inside the yard. No weapons display, people, horses, flags or writing. Ground footprint 15 by 12.

Ming Jiangnan discreet gaming house, original wuxia game architecture: compact two-storey dark-timber hall with white plaster sides, grey tiled roof, screened upstairs lattice windows, low small entrance porch and two visible wooden gaming tables just within an open ground-floor bay. No signs, lantern canopy or extravagant decoration. Ground footprint 10 by 8.

Ming Jiangnan wealthy merchant garden manor compound, unified original game courtyard: white lime perimeter wall, dark grey roofs, brown lattice-panel timber rear hall and side wing, small planted inner court with one ornamental tree and modest scholar's rock; elaborate but restrained, no pagoda or water feature. Clear perimeter footprint 16 by 13.

Ming Jiangnan princely residence hall compound module, original generalized design not a recreation of a named palace: formal large central hall and two low side halls inside a low white lime enclosure, muted ochre and burgundy timber rank accents, dark charcoal-grey tiled hip-and-gable roof with restrained ridge ornaments, pale stone main steps and balanced open forecourt. Do not use Forbidden-City yellow roof, Qing multicolour painted beams or enormous red wall. Footprint 22 by 18.

Ming Jiangnan Buddhist temple main hall, one dignified timber worship building with grey tiled hip-and-gable roof and restrained brown supporting brackets, plaster-white end walls, deep portico, open central door dimly showing only a generic altar silhouette, low pale stone base and front steps. No statues outside, garden, flags, writing or monks. Footprint 14 by 11.

Ming Jiangnan Buddhist landmark: slender five-storey octagonal brick-and-timber pagoda with dark grey gently upturned clay eaves, aged pale lime and grey-brick body, small recessed openings and modest dark timber galleries. Inspired by Jiangnan brick-and-wood pagoda typology, not an exact named monument. One thin square stone footprint 7 by 7 beneath octagonal body, NO thick pedestal. Full finial and base uncut.

Ming Jiangnan small city-gate watchmen's guardhouse, one low utilitarian white-plastered masonry room with dark grey clay gable roof, strong brown timber doorway, narrow side window and tiny recessed porch; this is a separate ordinary building, NOT an outer-city gate arch, wall segment, turret or palace. Thin stone sill, clear ground footprint 7 by 5.

Ming Jiangnan modest stable building, one low white-plastered back wall and dark timber open-front three-bay shelter with dark grey clay tile pitched roof, straw bundles, simple low timber stall partitions and empty feeding troughs; no horses or people. Restrained working courtyard only within thin ground footprint 9 by 7.
